The PDM groundwater extension

Source: R/groundwater_extension.R
groundwater_extension.Rd

Extends a linear, quadratic or cubic groundwater store as in the extended PDM of Moore and Bell (2002) and the PDM for PCs scientific guide (UKCEH, 2022, section 3 and Appendix B), for catchments with pumped abstractions, ephemeral streams and losses below or beyond the gauge.

Usage

groundwater_extension(
  store,
  ku = Inf,
  dbu = 0,
  alpha_b = 0,
  ca = 0,
  fa = 1,
  smax_b = 0,
  ys = 0,
  hw = 0
)

FlodeExtendedGroundwater(
  store = FlodePowerRouting(),
  ku = integer(0),
  dbu = integer(0),
  alpha_b = integer(0),
  ca = integer(0),
  fa = integer(0),
  smax_b = integer(0),
  ys = integer(0),
  hw = integer(0)
)

Arguments

store

A linear, quadratic or cubic groundwater store, from linear_routing(), quadratic_routing(), cubic_routing() or power_routing() with m 1, 2 or 3.

ku

Underflow time constant, h; Inf (the default) for no underflow.

dbu

Baseflow-underflow deficit, mm: how far below the baseflow outlet the underflow outlet lies.

alpha_b

Fraction of the store's outflow lost to springs outside the catchment; negative for an import. At most 1.

ca

Constant abstraction, mm/h.

fa

Factor on the recorded abstraction.

smax_b

Maximum groundwater storage, mm, for the deficit and well level.

ys

Well factor, m of water-table depth per mm of storage deficit (PDM for PCs wellfac): 1 / (1000 Sy) for a specific yield Sy; 0 (the default) for no well level.

hw

Well level datum: the height of the ground at the well, m.

Value

A FlodeExtendedGroundwater store.

Details

Abstraction and negative storage. The input to the store is recharge less abstraction, u = d - A, with A = cA + fA Ar where Ar is the recorded abstraction (Eq. 9). A negative input drains the store, and when it empties flow at the outlet stops: the time to cessation within the step, T', is exact for each store (Eqs. B.1, B.3 and B.5), and the storage at the end of that step is u (dt - T') (Eqs. B.2, B.4 and B.6). Below zero the storage changes by continuity alone, with no outflow, until recharge refills it and flow starts again for the rest of that step.

Underflow leaves through a lower outlet below the gauge, linearly in the water above it: qu = (S + Dbu) / ku while S > -Dbu (Eq. 10, with Dbu = Du - Sbmax, the baseflow-underflow deficit). Neither source states how underflow is integrated within a step. Here the store and both its outlets are integrated together, dS/dt = u - k max(S, 0)^m - qu, by RK4 with step doubling to the store's tolerances (rtol, atol), whatever its solver. Each outlet stops at its own threshold within the step, so neither draws the store below it, and the two share the water as the continuous equation does. (Before 0.26.0 the underflow was held at its start-of-step rate, which over a long step could drain the store well below its outlets.)

External springs. A fraction alpha_b of the store's outflow leaves the catchment as springs and the rest is baseflow at the outlet. A negative fraction brings water in: an inter-catchment exchange (scientific guide, section 4). The import is then -alpha_b times the store's release: the baseflow exceeds the release, the spring column is negative, and the water balance counts it as a gain. alpha_b must lie below 1; there is no lower limit in the model, and calibration searches -1 to 0.9 unless told otherwise.

Well level. The storage deficit is D = Sbmax - S (Eq. 8), in mm, and the depth to the water table W = Ys D (Eq. 11), in m, so Ys is metres of water table per mm of deficit: 1 / (1000 Sy) for an aquifer of specific yield Sy (0.02 for a specific yield of 5%). With the datum hw, the height of the ground at the well (m), the modelled well level is hw - W, in m. fit_well_level() fits Ys and hw to an observed well. (Before 0.27.0 the depth was divided by a further 1000, so modelled well levels barely moved.)

The exponential store cannot be extended: it needs positive flow at all times, so it cannot run dry (scientific guide, Appendices A and B).

Negative input. When abstraction exceeds recharge, the linear and quadratic stores cease flowing and drain by the exact published solutions (Eqs. B.1 to B.4). The cubic store follows its solver: with solver = "smith", Smith's method as published (Eqs. 4, 6 and 7); with the adaptive solver, the continuous equation integrated to the store's tolerances, through the moment flow ceases and on into deficit by continuity. (Before 0.26.0 the adaptive cubic store switched to Smith's method whenever its input was negative.) Below zero there is no outflow and the store changes by continuity until it refills, then routes by its own solver for the rest of the step.

Models with the extension run in the compiled engine, like the standard model, and give the same results as the step-by-step R loop. Starting from a flow (initial_state_from_flow()) and state correction use the R loop. Abstraction enters as a forcing column abstraction, mm per step over the catchment.

References

Moore, R.J. and Bell, V.A. (2002). Incorporation of groundwater losses and well level data in rainfall-runoff models illustrated using the PDM. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 6(1), 25-38. UKCEH (2022). A Guide to the PDM Rainfall-Runoff Model, in PDM for PCs, version 3.0.3.

Examples

store <- groundwater_extension(cubic_routing(5000), ku = 12000, dbu = 400, ca = 0.002,
                               smax_b = 1600, ys = 0.02, hw = 84)
cfg <- pdm_presets("standard")
cfg$groundwater$extension <- list(ku = 12000, dbu = 400, ca = 0.002)
model <- pdm_from_config(cfg)
